newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes firmer, Oman differentials healthier.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes firmer, Oman differentials healthier.

text.p: Crude prices in Asia were firmer on Tuesday with Tapis prices marching higher and Oman differentials moving into a premium.
The Brent/Dubai spread for active-month December widened to $2.45/$2.60 from a day-earlier $2.15/$2.30 and London's late $2.40/$2.45.

At the same time, Dubai intermonth spreads widened to 50/60 cents for November/December and 44/48 for December/January and January/February. This compared with 42/47 cents for November/December and 41/46 for December/January and January/February on Monday.
Overnight, the December Brent/Dubai was traded a $2.32 between a European major and a U.S. refiner and at $2.35 between another European major and the same U.S. refiner.
November paper Tapis rose to $24.30/$24.50 on Tuesday from $23.95/$24.15 a day-earlier, also supported by firmer Brent and NYMEX futures prices.
Brokers said two traders exchanged 100,000 barrels on paper at $24.33 per barrel. The seller of the outright also sold a November/December spread at 36 cents to a Wall Street trader, they said.

November Brent futures in London overnight hit a fresh five-year high for the front-month contract of $24.50 per barrel. SIMEX Tuesday closed down 17 cents at $24.32 and London continued the down trend.
Traders said a major bought a cargo of Oman at MPM +2 cents from a Japanese trader, the highest trade for a full cargo for November. Traders said they expected Oman to maintain modest premiums.
Two Nanhei light cargos were traded around flat to APPI Tapis quotes. A 450,000 barrel cargo went to a U.S. major and 600,000 barrels went to an Indonesian buyer.
